questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial clause.

A) On the table, the book was left by her.
B) Never have I seen such a beautiful garden.
C) So fast did she run that she broke the record.
D) If only we had known about the party earlier!
options: On the table, the book was left by her.
Never have I seen such a beautiful garden.
So fast did she run that she broke the record.
If only we had known about the party earlier!
questions.answer: So fast did she run that she broke the record.

questions.question:
Which of the following sentences correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight the specific location of the event?

A) It was in London that the conference was held.
B) London was where the conference was held.
C) The conference was held in London, wasn't it?
D) The conference, held in London, was a great success.
options: It was in London that the conference was held.
London was where the conference was held.
The conference was held in London, wasn't it?
The conference, held in London, was a great success.
questions.answer: It was in London that the conference was held.

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly uses the third type of conditional sentence to discuss a hypothetical scenario in the past.

A) If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
B) If I had studied harder, I would be passing the exam now.
C) If I had studied harder, I would have been able to pass the exam.
D) If I had studied harder, I would pass the exam.
options: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would be passing the exam now.
If I had studied harder, I would have been able to pass the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would pass the exam.
questions.answer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a formal recommendation?

A) I suggest that the committee members meet tomorrow.
B) It is recommended that the committee members meet tomorrow.
C) We recommend that the committee members meet tomorrow.
D) The committee members are recommended to meet tomorrow.
options: I suggest that the committee members meet tomorrow.
It is recommended that the committee members meet tomorrow.
We recommend that the committee members meet tomorrow.
The committee members are recommended to meet tomorrow.
questions.answer: It is recommended that the committee members meet tomorrow.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly demonstrates ellipsis, where a word is omitted but understood from context.

A) John likes apples, and so does Mary.
B) John likes apples, and Mary, too.
C) John likes apples, and Mary does too.
D) John likes apples, and Mary also.
options: John likes apples, and so does Mary.
John likes apples, and Mary, too.
John likes apples, and Mary does too.
John likes apples, and Mary also.
questions.answer: John likes apples, and so does Mary.
